title: Capacity verification runbook and tenant-fidelity gauge for Dedicated throughput certification
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Single-source runbook and measurement spec to certify Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees for customers. Covers a reproducible load generation suite that emulates realistic tenant mixes, autoscaler exercise scenarios, kernel/quantization variants, telemetry requirements, and an acceptance checklist customers sign off on. Intention is to create a repeatable, auditable path from internal load runs to a customer-facing acceptance test that yields a simple PASS/FAIL report and a performance evidence bundle for contracting.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook executes end-to-end against a reserved Dedicated pool with a reproducible tenant mix and produces a perf_report.json containing per-tenant P50/P95/P99 latencies, token/sec, and error rates
Autoscaler scenarios: steady-state, 3x burst, microburst (1s-10s), and sustained ramp to 80% capacity; autoscaler must remain within configured scaling bounds and not trigger unsafe restarts
Tail-latency SLO: P99 < 350ms for 2k-token requests under defined workload mix (or explicit customer SLA override), with no more than 0.1% 5xx errors
Tenant interference gauge: noisy-tenant injection experiments do not cause baseline tenant latency degradation > 15% in accepted runs
Artifacts: GitHub PR linking the run config, Grafana dashboard snapshot, perf_report.json, raw traces (jaeger ids), and a signed customer acceptance doc must be present
Security: test data must use synthetic PII-safe prompts and run within the customer's VPC when validating a Private deployment
test_plan: Prepare dedicated pool with target machine type and quantization profile (e.g., a100-80gb, int8-qkv) and pin model version
Provision a telemetry collector and ephemeral Grafana folder for the run; verify streaming traces and token-level accounting
Deploy load-generation clients in three regions to simulate geo-distribution and network variance
Execute baseline probe (single-tenant ramp) to capture cold-start behavior and KV cache warmup curve
Run multi-tenant fidelity experiment using the Tenant Mix Matrix (see attachments) and capture outputs
Orchestrate autoscaler stress sequences: ramp-up, ramp-down, sustained-high, microbursts, and node-swap
Run failure-injection sweep: simulate a node OOM, NVLink flake, and transient storage I/O stall and observe graceful degradation/fallback behavior
Collect artifacts, generate perf_report.json, and open customer acceptance PR with evidence bundle

expected_results: perf_report.json schema is valid and contains per-tenant breakdowns
P95 latency drift across tenant-noise scenarios < 15% versus baseline
Autoscaler acts within configured bounds and does not produce >3x frequent oscillations in a 30m window
No data plane panics or model corruptions; 5xx error spikes must be investigable and tied to a causal event in traces
customer_onboarding_flow: 1) Pre-run review call: present run config, SLA targets, and required IAM roles
2) Dry-run with synthetic traffic and readout of dashboards
3) Formal acceptance run scheduled in coordination with customer's SRE
4) Post-run review: share perf_report.json and working set of traces
5) Customer signs performance acceptance that becomes part of the Dedicated contract
risks_mitigation: Risk: autoscaler instability under weird mixes — Mitigation: implement hysteresis and max-frequency controls in policy and include rollback step
Risk: telemetry gaps during high throughput — Mitigation: local buffering for prometheus exporters and a secondary log shipper
Risk: customer misconfigured model pinning causing performance regressions — Mitigation: enforce compatibility checks in run-config validation and refuse runs until satisfied
Risk: cost overruns for long runs — Mitigation: hard budget caps in terraform quotas and automated teardown on budget breach
